title: Benedict XVI (2005–2013)
hookLine: a quiet theologian whose first encyclical was God is love

cards: A new pope's first encyclical is watched closely: his first long letter to the whole Church, read for a program.
This one came from a man who had spent his life as a professor and then as the Vatican's guardian of doctrine. Some expected rules. Its Latin title was three words: Deus caritas est.
God is love. It opens with a line from the first letter of John, and then does something some readers didn't expect from a strict theologian.
It talks about eros, the love of desire, and agape, the love that gives itself away, and says the two belong together.

teach.b: His name was Joseph Ratzinger; as pope he took the name Benedict. First, the scholar. He was a theologian before he was a bishop, a writer of books, more at home at a desk than on a balcony.
He had worked on yesterday's Catechism, and for a long time he guarded Catholic teaching in Rome, which earned him critics as well as admirers.

teach.h: THE NAME OF A MONK AND A PEACE POPE.
teach.b: Second, the name: Benedict, the monk of Nursia whose rule shaped monasteries across Europe, and Benedict the Fifteenth, a pope who pleaded for peace in a world war. Third, the letter.
The first letter of John, in the Douay-Rheims, uses an older English word for love: "God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God, and God in him." Charity there isn't a donation.
It's the Latin caritas, love itself. Benedict starts there and turns practical: if God is love, the Church's care for the poor and the sick isn't a side activity.
It belongs to what the Church is, as much as the sacraments and the preaching of the word. Fourth, the disagreement. Some remember a brilliant, gentle teacher.
Others remember the strict guardian of doctrine, or a papacy troubled by scandal. Both are part of the record. But his first letter to the whole Church had a three-word title.
And that ends the week: from forgiving the gunman, through Assisi, World Youth Day, the Day of Pardon, the abuse crisis and the Catechism, to a pope whose first word to the Church was love.

how: Catholics read the first letter of John at Mass at various points in the year, and parishes and charities sometimes study Deus caritas est for its teaching that care for the poor belongs to the Church's own life.

games.q: you're a new pope, known as a strict guardian of doctrine. you have one first letter to the whole Church. what is it about?
o: God is love, and what that asks of the Church.
games.why: he wrote Deus caritas est: God is love, joining eros and agape, and calling the Church's charity part of its very life.

practice: Say the line slowly, in the old words: God is charity, and he that abideth in charity abideth in God.

Then put a face on it, someone who loved you when nothing was in it for them, a neighbor, a friend, a stranger who helped, and stay with them a while. If you pray, thank God for them; if not, simply be grateful.

orig.note: Latin: God is love, from 1 John 4 in the Vulgate, and the title of Benedict XVI's first encyclical.
